Start with an input file from the maintained OPALX regression suite. Those
inputs are executable specifications and are checked continuously against the
current parser and physics implementation.

## Run a small regression input {#regression-smoke-test}

From the root of the OPALX checkout, after building the serial executable:

```bash
export OPALX_EXE="$PWD/build_serial/src/opalx"
git clone https://github.com/OPALX-project/regression-tests-x.git
mkdir -p run-drift
cp regression-tests-x/RegressionTests/Drift-1-fromfile/Drift-1-fromfile.in run-drift/
cp regression-tests-x/RegressionTests/Drift-1-fromfile/distr-gauss.txt run-drift/
cd run-drift
"$OPALX_EXE" Drift-1-fromfile.in --info 2
```

This case tracks 1,000 electrons through a drift with self-fields disabled
(`FIELDSOLVER, TYPE=NONE`). Keep `distr-gauss.txt` beside the input: the
particle distribution is read from that file. The run writes
`Drift-1-fromfile.stat`; check that it completes successfully and produces
statistics.

This is a **smoke test**, not an automated numerical regression comparison.
The regression repository also supplies a `.rt` file defining checked metrics
and tolerances, and a `reference/` directory with reference results. See the
[regression repository]({{< meta regression-tests-source-url >}}/README.md)
for its structure and the dashboard below for current results. Do not
regenerate references merely to make a failing check pass.

The regression repository evolves independently of OPALX releases. Record its
revision with `git -C ../regression-tests-x rev-parse HEAD` when reporting a
result; its default branch is not a frozen 1.0.0 test suite.

## Launch on a GPU


For a multi-GPU run, map each MPI rank to a device:

```bash
srun /path/to/build_cuda/src/opalx example.in \
  --info 2 --kokkos-map-device-id-by=mpi_rank
```

## What to check

- The startup banner identifies the build and execution backend.
- Parser errors name the statement and location that could not be read.
- Statistics and particle outputs depend on the input-file options and output
  commands.
- A nonzero exit status means the run did not complete successfully.

The [regression-test dashboard]({{< meta regression-tests-url >}}) shows which
inputs currently pass. Input-file compatibility is still being cataloged, so a
regression input is safer than copying an example from the historical OPAL
manual. Continue with the three complete [Worked Input Files](worked-inputs.qmd)
for progressively more detailed starting points.
